\begin{abstract}
Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant metric and a
nonidentity central element $z$, and equip a finite hypercubic lattice with
the heat-kernel plaquette action at time $t$.  Around any full-degree link in
dimension $d\geq2$, write $m=2(d-1)$.  We construct an admissible assignment
of all other links for which $m-1$ incident staples are trivial and one equals
$z$.  The resulting one-link conditional density is
\[
  Z_t^{-1}p_t(U)^{m-1}p_t(z^{-1}U)\,\Haar .
\]
Its small-time rate is
$F_z(U)=(m-1)\dist(\one,U)^2+\dist(z,U)^2$.  A metric barycenter identity
shows that every minimizer lies one $m$th of the way from $\one$ to $z$.
Consequently, if the frustrated plaquette is called good inside radius
$\rho<(m-1)\dist(\one,z)/m$, then
\[
 \lim_{t\downarrow0}2t\log\Prob_t(\text{good}\mid\text{frustrated boundary})
 =-m\left(\frac{m-1}{m}\dist(\one,z)-\rho\right)^2.
\]
The bad probability therefore tends to one, uniformly on an open,
positive-Haar-measure neighborhood of the constructed boundary.  We also
show that the associated single-link Dobrushin row sum exceeds one for all
sufficiently small $t$.  Thus boundary-uniform rare-defect domination, and
the corresponding Dobrushin criterion, cannot provide weak-coupling control
in these link coordinates.  The result is a finite-lattice obstruction to
those quantifiers; it is not a statement about Gibbs uniqueness, continuum
Yang--Mills theory, confinement, or a mass gap.
\end{abstract}
